headline: Comp sales and margins expand while buybacks accelerate
summary_short: Revenue rose 11.1% year over year to $3.16 billion as comparable sales grew 5.3%, while gross margin expanded to 40.1% on lower shrink and higher merchandise margin, lifting net income 11.6% to $340.5 million.
summary_long: Net sales rose 11.1% y/y to $3.16 billion on 5.3% comparable-sales growth (ticket +3.7%, transactions +1.6%), the Space NK acquisition, and new stores. Gross margin expanded 100bp to 40.1% on lower shrink and higher merchandise margin. SG&A rose to 25.8% of sales, mainly Space NK and strategic investments, partly offset by advertising leverage. Net income rose 11.6% to $340.5 million; diluted EPS rose 15.5% to $7.74, helped by a lower effective tax rate (23.9% vs 24.6%) from discounted federal tax-credit purchases. Ulta repurchased $545.3 million of stock, with $1.3 billion remaining under authorization; cash fell to $166.3 million on buybacks and inventory build. No forward guidance was disclosed.

drivers.explanation: 5.3% comparable-sales growth (ticket +3.7%, transactions +1.6%), the Space NK acquisition, and new store openings drove the increase.
Margin expansion was primarily due to lower inventory shrink and higher merchandise margin.
Growth mainly reflects the gross-profit increase, partially offset by higher SG&A, higher income tax expense, and lower interest income.

SG&A deleverage from the Space NK acquisition and strategic enterprise investments was partly offset by advertising leverage; effective tax rate fell to 23.9% on discounted federal tax-credit purchases.
